question_text: The lengths of steel rods cut by a machine are normally distributed with mean $13.8\text{ cm}$. It is found that 1.5% of all rods are less than $13.2\text{ cm}$ long.

subparts.stem: Find the probability that a randomly selected rod has length between 13.2 cm and 13.8 cm.

mark_breakdown.desc: Using properties of the normal distribution to express the interval probability as a difference of cumulative probabilities
Correctly calculating the probability to obtain 0.485

subparts.solution: Let the length of a randomly selected steel rod be $X\text{ cm}$. So, $X \sim \text{N}(13.8, \sigma^2)$.\\\begin{aligned} \text{P}(13.2 < X < 13.8) &= \text{P}(X < 13.8) - \text{P}(X < 13.2) \\ &= 0.5 - 0.015 \\ &= 0.485 \end{aligned}

ai_explanation.concept_rule: For a normal distribution $X \sim \text{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$, $\text{P}(X < \mu) = 0.5$ due to symmetry about the mean. The probability of an interval is given by $\text{P}(a < X < b) = \text{P}(X < b) - \text{P}(X < a)$.
step_by_step: Recognize that the upper limit $13.8$ is the mean $\mu$, so $\text{P}(X < 13.8) = 0.5$.
Subtract the cumulative probability of the lower bound from that of the upper bound: $0.5 - 0.015 = 0.485$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting that the normal distribution is symmetrical about $\mu$, or confusing $P(X < 13.8)$ with a standard normal value.

subparts.stem: Find the standard deviation of rod lengths produced by this machine.

mark_breakdown.desc: Using inverse normal to find the critical value $z \approx -2.17$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: To find an unknown parameter of a normal distribution from a known tail probability, standardize to $Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma} \sim \text{N}(0, 1)$ and use the inverse normal function.
step_by_step: Use the inverse normal distribution with area $0.015$, mean $0$, and standard deviation $1$ to find $z \approx -2.17009$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Omitting the negative sign on the $z$-score for a probability in the lower tail ($< 0.5$), which would lead to an invalid negative standard deviation.
